text:
We often judge the health of open source projects by their contributor count, but this metric is deeply misleading. A project might boast hundreds of contributors, yet if 95% of them are merely fixing typos in documentation or updating README files, the core codebase remains fragile and under-resourced. 

True sustainability isn't found in vanity numbers; it’s found in the density of high-impact code maintainers. We need to stop funding "popularity" and start funding the critical, unglamorous work that actually keeps the infrastructure running.
